title: Tenant-aware kernel hygiene and cold-start mitigation runbook for FlashAttention v3 rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational and engineering plan (a.k.a. "kernel hygiene") that prevents FlashAttention v3 regressions from causing tenant-facing latency or correctness incidents during canary and ramp. Deliverables: tenant-scoped microprober, short-circuit gating rules, an operator rollback runbook, and automated safety checks that run prior to allowing v3 kernels to serve production traffic for a tenant.
background: Recent v3 ramps exposed two classes of problems: (1) tenant cold-starts where certain input shapes and prompt prefixes cause v3 to select a kernel variant with unexpectedly higher latency, and (2) intermittent numerical noise on a handful of quantized models that only appeared under mixed-batch prefill patterns. Existing mitigation (global rollback or broad prefills) is too blunt and causes cost and availability regressions for unaffected tenants.
goals: Provide per-tenant safety checks so we can allow v3 for tenants that empirically benefit from it
Automate a short microbenchmark run that validates kernel performance and numerical parity before traffic is routed to v3 for a tenant
Ship an operator-facing rollback/runbook with exact timed steps and playbook checks to remediate a regression within 15 minutes
Instrument telemetry to detect kernel-induced latency or token-quality regressions within 5 minutes of first-serving
scope: Implement tenant microprober service, integrate gating into rollout pipeline, add telemetry alerts and a documented runbook for oncall. Add lightweight canary traffic harness to exercise long-context/mixed-batch prefill shapes.
out_of_scope: Large-scale model re-training, changes to model weights, or full-stack redesign of kernel selection heuristics beyond adding gating and probes.
success_metrics: Reduction in v3-related P1 incidents by 80% for tenants enrolled in tenant-hygiene
Time-to-detect kernel-induced latency regressions reduced to <= 5 minutes
Average rollback time across incidents <= 15 minutes when runbook followed
acceptance_criteria: Microprober runs complete within 10s per tenant and produce a small JSON verdict (pass|warn|fail)
Gating prevents v3 assignment for tenants with a 'fail' verdict and marks tenants 'deferred' in rollout UI
Operator runbook has step-by-step commands and validated playbook checks, and a tabletop drill has been executed with SRE and Runtime leads
At least two internal tenants (staging + one high-throughput internal customer) are on the new flow and show no degradation after 48h
implementation_plan: 1) Design microprobe: short end-to-end run that loads model variant, runs a set of canonical prompts (1-2 tokens warm, long-context prefill, mixed-batch), collects latency and token-delta stats
2) Build lightweight microprober service (Go) that can be invoked from rollout pipeline and Canvas canary controller
3) Define gating rules: thresholds for p50/p95 latency delta, and token-level divergence metric (logprob delta) for numerical noise
4) Integrate gating into rollout orchestration: if microprobe returns fail -> keep tenant on v2 and mark in UI, if warn -> enable extra telemetry sampling
5) Add telemetry queries and alerts (Grafana/Tempo/StatsD) for early detection and annotate with tenant metadata
6) Write the operator runbook and run a 30-minute tabletop drill with SRE and PM
7) Gradual rollout: opt-in internal tenants -> limited external tenants -> broader rollout once stable
test_plan: Unit tests for microprober parsing and verdict logic
Integration test that injects synthetic kernel slowdowns and verifies gating blocks v3 assignment
Canary e2e test that runs microprobe and then sends small production-like traffic while monitoring telemetry hooks
Tabletop drill: simulate regression and follow runbook; measure time to rollback and restore
telemetry_queries: alert: kernel.latency.delta_above_threshold (compare v3 variant to baseline)
metric: kernel.token_divergence.per_tenant (avg logprob delta over sample prompts)
risks: Microprobe false negatives: some failure modes only surface after sustained traffic patterns
Probe adds small latency to onboarding flow if run synchronously; must be async or very short
Overly conservative gates may block performance gains for many tenants
Edge-case numerical divergences might not be captured by our canonical prompts
mitigation_steps: Start with opt-in internal tenants and expand after 1 week of stable signals
Keep probe light (<=10s) and run it in parallel to other onboarding tasks; allow async verdict to update routing after first few requests
Tune thresholds based on early telemetry and add a 'warn' tier for gradual exposure
Collect sampled token sequences and add them to a replay harness for deeper offline analysis
